key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produced denser, harder Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings with 27% lower sliding wear volume than conventional radial-feed APS, but little improvement in 90° erosion.
engineering_relevance: HV-APS is a promising option for sliding-wear-resistant steel coatings, although its benefit should not be assumed for normal-impact erosion.
method: Sprayed Metco 5241 Cr₃C₂–NiCr powder onto S235 steel using conventional APS and supersonic HV-APS.
Compared coating microstructure, phase composition, porosity, and microhardness.
Evaluated erosion at 90° impact and ball-on-disc sliding wear under a 30 N load.
evidence_signal: HV-APS versus APS yielded 6.16% versus 11.99% porosity, 1141 versus 897 HV0.2 hardness, and 2.85 versus 3.90 mm³ wear volume, while specific erosion rates were similar at 0.19 versus 0.20 mg/g.
watch_item: The comparison changes both torch technology and powder-feed geometry, so the improvement cannot be attributed to axial feeding alone.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
